topic: Pete Hegseth: formal House impeachment, office departure, Senate conviction and succession

definitions.formal_house_impeachment: U.S. House adopts at least one article of impeachment against Pete Hegseth. An introduction, procedural vote, or committee referral alone does not qualify.
definitions.departure: Pete Hegseth permanently ceases to hold U.S. Secretary of Defense/Secretary of War office; excludes temporary absence. Announcement alone does not count for this analysis unless effective by cutoff.
definitions.senate_conviction: U.S. Senate votes by the constitutionally required two-thirds of members present to convict Hegseth on at least one article.
definitions.successor: First individual Trump publicly nominates as a permanent, Senate-confirmed replacement after Hegseth permanently departs, conditional on a nomination being made by Dec. 31, 2027. Acting officers are excluded.

market_context_not_exactly_comparable.note: Market pages may reflect different refresh times. Some contracts count announcements whereas the KAHRELUM departure event requires effective departure; read rules before comparing prices.

analysis_notes: These are subjective judgment probabilities, not a validated KAHRELUM model output or certified track record.
War-powers crossover votes are not the same as votes for impeachment.
The House GOP retains procedural means to delay, table, or refer Massie's resolution.
Senate conviction is substantially harder than impeachment; departure is more likely to occur through White House personnel action.
The 2026 election changes control in January 2027, not November 2026.
Successor probabilities concern first publicly named permanent nominee, not the acting secretary and not confirmation odds.
All reported allegations are contested and have not been adjudicated in this analysis.
